title: Hybrid AINWP Multi-Model Forecast Blending System
department: National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF)
description:
• Problem Statement Different forecasting systems perform differently depending on region, season, lead time and weather situation. Physical NWP models, ensemble forecasts and AI/ML weather models may each have strengths under different conditions. Therefore, there is a need for an intelligent blending system that can dynamically combine multiple forecasts.
The challenge is to develop a hybrid AI–NWP blending framework that assigns adaptive weights to different forecast sources based on historical skill, forecast lead time, region, season and weather regime. The final product should provide an optimized forecast for rainfall, temperature, wind and extreme weather indicators.
Expected Outcome - Description
• Dynamically blended forecast - Best-combined forecast from multiple model sources
• Model weight maps - Indication of which model is more reliable for each region/lead time
• Improved forecast skill - Better performance than individual models
• Extreme weather guidance - Improved signals for heavy rainfall, heat wave and high-wind events
• Operational workflow - Automated script/dashboard for routine forecast blending
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, ml applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (4/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Hybrid AI-NWP Multi-Model Forecast Blending System

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that intelligently combines predictions from multiple different weather forecasting models, physics-based, ensemble, AI, picking the best one for each region, season, and situation instead of relying on just one.
overview.why_it_matters: No single forecasting model is best everywhere, all the time. Smart blending gets consistently better forecasts than any individual model alone.
pain_points: Different forecasting systems perform differently depending on region, season, lead time, and weather situation.
No intelligent system currently blends multiple forecast sources adaptively.
Forecasters must manually judge which model to trust in a given situation without systematic guidance.
overview.background: Physical NWP models, ensemble forecasts, and AI/ML weather models each have different strengths under different conditions, but there's no intelligent system dynamically blending them based on historical performance context.
overview.whats_being_asked: A hybrid AI-NWP blending framework assigning adaptive weights to different forecast sources based on historical skill, lead time, region, season, and weather regime.
expected_solution: Dynamically blended forecast combining multiple model sources.
Model weight/reliability maps by region and lead time.
Improved forecast skill versus any individual model.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate-High. Multi-model ensemble blending with adaptive, context-dependent weighting is a real, established-but-sophisticated meteorological technique (similar to super-ensemble approaches), genuine technical value.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate. Achievable using historical forecast performance data across multiple model sources and a weighting/blending algorithm.

competitive_landscape.note: Technical meta-forecasting PS similar in spirit to SIH26079, a narrower field appealing to teams with forecast-verification interest.

innovation.note: Adaptive, context-dependent multi-model blending is a real, sophisticated technique beyond simple averaging.

invention.note: Achievable using historical performance data and established blending/weighting approaches.

technical_feasibility.note: Public forecasts from multiple model sources (various NWP and AI weather models) and historical verification data exist.

impact_and_benefits.tag: Real but Modest in Demo Scope
impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine operational value if deployed, though a 36-hour demo will necessarily be a scoped proof-of-concept.

architecture.note: A weighting/blending layer sitting atop multiple forecast sources, well-understood ensemble pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow, genuinely achievable with real data, though requires access to multiple distinct forecast sources for genuine blending (not just claiming to blend when only using one source). Scope to 2-3 real forecast sources for a credible demonstration.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Public data from multiple distinct forecast sources genuinely exists, supporting a real (not simulated) blending demonstration.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Claiming to blend 'AI/ML weather models' alongside NWP without actually sourcing a real distinct AI-based forecast product would weaken the core premise, ensure you have genuinely distinct sources to blend.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Source at least 2-3 genuinely distinct forecast products (e.g. two different NWP models plus one public AI weather forecast product) rather than claiming multi-model blending with only one real source.

idea_0_4: Source 2-3 genuinely distinct public forecast products for your test region and period (different NWP models, or an NWP model plus a public AI weather forecast).
Source historical verification data to establish each source's regional/seasonal skill baseline.
Split: one person on data sourcing/alignment, one on the adaptive weighting/blending model.
prototype_4_22: Build your data pipeline aligning multiple forecast sources for the same region/time.
Build your adaptive weighting logic, assigning weights based on historical skill by region/season/lead-time.
Start computing your blended forecast output.
integration_22_30: Test your blended forecast against actual observed outcomes for your test period, comparing skill against each individual source.
Build the model-weight visualization showing which source is favored where and when.
Refine your weighting logic based on validation results.
polish_30_36: Build a clear dashboard showing the blended forecast, individual source forecasts, and weight maps.
Rehearse presenting your validation results, blended skill versus best individual model, real numbers.
Prepare to discuss how this would scale to a full operational multi-model blending workflow.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your blended forecast genuinely outperforming every individual source model on your validated test period, that head-to-head comparison, blend versus best single model, is the concrete proof this PS is asking for.

strengths: Public data from multiple genuinely distinct forecast sources exists for real demonstration.
Well-understood ensemble/blending pattern with real technical sophistication in the adaptive weighting.
weaknesses: Requires genuinely sourcing multiple distinct forecast products, not just one relabeled source.
Real operational-scale blending across many sources isn't achievable at demo scope, requires scoping to 2-3 sources.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with real effort on sourcing genuinely distinct forecast products.
team_fit.approach: Confirm access to at least 2-3 genuinely distinct real forecast sources before committing to this PS, the entire premise depends on genuine multi-source blending.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly interpreting historical skill patterns to inform sensible adaptive weighting (not overfitting to noise in limited historical data), that requires real statistical and meteorological judgment.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded blending system trained on limited historical data without careful validation could overfit to noise, producing weights that look sophisticated but don't generalize to new forecast situations.

data_resource_availability.status: Public data from multiple distinct forecast sources (different NWP models, some public AI weather forecast products) genuinely exists and is accessible.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If a genuine AI-model forecast source isn't accessible, blend across multiple distinct NWP model outputs, which are more readily available, and be clear about which source types you actually blended.

judge_qna.question: What forecast sources did you actually blend, and are they genuinely distinct models?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Name your specific sources directly and confirm they're genuinely independent forecast systems, not variations of the same underlying model relabeled.
judge_qna.follow_up: How correlated are your source models' errors, does blending genuinely add value if they tend to fail in similar ways?

judge_qna.question: How does your adaptive weighting avoid overfitting to a limited historical validation period?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your approach to avoiding overfitting, using a reasonably long historical period, cross-validation, or regularization in your weighting scheme, and be honest about the limitations of whatever validation period you had access to.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would your weights need to be recalibrated as models are updated or new ones are added?
